cs.label: [section] Požadavky na ukončení:
cs.content: Pro úspěšné splnění laboratorního cvičení je nutno absolvovat všechny úlohy včetně úspěšného odevzdání protokolů a splnit zápočtový test alespoň na 75%. K závěrečné zkoušce je student připuštěn až po udělení zápočtu z laboratorního cvičení. Závěrečná zkouška má písemnou a ústní část. Třiceti minutový písemný test obsahuje čtyři okruhy otázek, které musí být zodpovězeny minimálně z 50 %. Následující ústní zkouška obsahuje 3 zkušební otázky z tematických okruhů uvedených v sylabu předmětu (každá otázka musí být alespoň částečně zodpovězena).

en.label: [section] Aim of the course and learning outcomes:
en.content: The course deepens knowledge of the composition and organisation of living systems. Learn the basics of enzymology and the principles of metabolic and energy transformations in organisms. Master the basics of biochemistry and acquire the skills to apply new knowledge in the study of related professional subjects.

en.label: [section] Course content:
en.content: 1.Substance composition of organisms (allowance 4/0) a.Water. Proteins. Nucleic acids.b.Carbohydrates. Lipids.c.Metabolic intermediates.d.Biogenic elements.2.Vitamins as components of enzyme cofactors (allowance 2/0) a.Major water-soluble and fat-soluble vitamins.b.Vitamin-like substances and anti-vitamins.3.Biocatalysis (allowance 4/0) a.Structure of enzyme molecules.b.Localization of enzymes and their forms of occurrence.c.Mechanism of action of enzymes.d.Effect of reaction conditions on enzyme efficiency.e.Regulation of enzyme activity.f.Classification and nomenclature of enzymes, expression of catalytic activity.g.Laboratory and industrial applications of enzymes.4.Principles of metabolic and energy transformation in organisms (allowance 2/0) a.Catabolism and anabolism.b.Energetics of biochemical reactions.c.Chemical energy carriers.d.Respiratory chain and oxidative phosphorylation.e.Citrate cycle and its modifications.f.Glyoxylate cycle.5.Carbohydrate metabolism I (allowance 2/0) a.Main pathway of carbohydrate breakdown - glycolysisb.Pentose phosphate cycle.c.Pyruvate conversion under anaerobic conditions, types of fermentation, regulation and energy balance.d.Carbohydrate biosynthesis (conversion of pyruvate to glucose, biosynthesis of glucose from other precursors).6.Carbohydrate metabolism II (allowance 2/0) a.Photosynthesis. Light and dark phases of photosynthesis.b.Calvin cycle and Hatch-Slack cycle.c.Photorespiration - location and significance.d.Assimilatory nitrate reduction and sulfate reduction.7.Lipid metabolism (allowance 2/0) a.Metabolism of triacylglycerols and fatty acids.b.Biosynthesis of energy reserve compounds.c.Biosynthesis, importance and function of steroidal substances.8.Metabolism of nitrogenous compounds I (allowance 2/0) a.Degradation of amino acids.b.Detoxification of ammonia - ornithine (ureogenetic) cycle, glutamine formation.c.Degradation of purines and pyrimidines.9.Metabolism of nitrogenous compounds II (allowance 2/0) a.Disorders of nitrogen metabolism.b.Proteosynthesis.c.Structure and function of nucleic acids.10.Metabolism of nitrogenous compounds III (allowance 2/0) a.Mechanism of genetic information transfer and their changes.b.Biosynthesis of peptide chains.c.Proteolysis.11.Secondary metabolism (allowance 2/0) a.Secondary metabolites and their importanceb.Chemical structure and biosynthesis of secondary metabolites.12.Principles of biochemical regulation (allowance 2/0) a.Intracellular regulation (regulation of protein production, metabolic regulation).b.Neurohormonal regulation.c.Hormones and their action.d.Plant hormones and their mechanism of action.13.Practical laboratory exercises (allowance 0/28) a.Techniques of sampling biological material and its preparation for biochemical analysis.b.Main biochemical methods.c.Study of vitamins.d.Study of lipids and nucleic acids.e.Study of proteins.f.Study of enzymes.

en.label: [section] Assessment methods:
en.content: For successful completion of the laboratory exercise it is necessary to complete all tasks including successful submission of protocols and to pass the credit test at least 75%. The student is admitted to the final examination only after the credit for the laboratory exercise has been awarded. The final examination has a written and an oral part. The thirty-minute written test contains four sets of questions that must be answered by at least 50%. The subsequent oral examination contains 3 examination questions from the topics listed in the course syllabus (each question must be at least partially answered).
